summary:
Our project is an interactive storytelling experience that explores the technology and equipment NASA used to explore the Moon and Mars, including hardware that remains on these worlds today.

Chapter 1, “The First Trip to the Moon,” tells the story of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, which helped astronauts land on the Moon during humanity’s first crewed lunar landing. The chapter explores its purpose, technology, journey, and legacy.

Chapter 2, “The Trip to Mars,” follows Spirit, one of NASA’s early Mars rovers. We present Spirit’s journey across Mars, the technology that allowed it to operate on another planet, and the scientific discoveries it made.

By combining historical facts with visual storytelling, our project makes space exploration easier to understand and helps audiences connect with the machines that made these missions possible.
details:
Our project, “Left Behind: The Untold Stories of NASA’s Spacecraft,” is an interactive educational website that brings past NASA missions and their forgotten hardware to life through storytelling.

The website currently contains two chapters. Chapter 1 follows Apollo 11’s Lunar Module descent stage, “Descent,” from its journey to the Moon to the moment it was left behind at Tranquility Base. Chapter 2 follows Spirit, one of NASA’s early Mars rovers, and its journey across the Martian surface. The project combines fictional storytelling with real mission facts and NASA sources, helping users understand the purpose, technology, and achievements of these machines.

The main benefit is making complex space history easier and more engaging for school-age audiences. Instead of simply reading technical facts, users experience each mission as a story and can then explore the real science and engineering behind it.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI assistance from Codex and Canva for visual storytelling.

Our team focused on accuracy, accessibility, storytelling, visual design, and making historical spacecraft feel interesting and memorable. The project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration while showing how past NASA technology helped expand humanity’s knowledge of the Moon and Mars.
